subject: health
title: Application or project: asking and receiving permission
essentialQuestion: How can understanding relationships, communication, and consent foundations help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?
materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool
keyPoints: Permission must be clear and specific to the activity; silence, uncertainty, or an earlier yes is not permission now, and either person can change their answer.
A safe communication plan states the limit clearly, recognizes pressure or danger, identifies an exit, and brings in adult or professional support when direct engagement is unsafe.
For asking and receiving permission, a strong response distinguishes fact from assumption, uses a fictional or public case, and includes a safe next step or appropriate source of support.
privacySafeScenario: Practice and record several assertive, respectful communication scripts using fictional situations.
studentTask: Annotate a supplied fictional exchange about asking and receiving permission: underline the stated limit, circle any pressure or respectful check-in, and write a two-sentence response that states a boundary plus a safe next step. Add when a trusted adult should enter the plan.
knowledgeCheck: In two or three sentences, explain the most important distinction in asking and receiving permission; use one lesson fact and name the evidence, safety check, or support route that makes the explanation dependable.
completionCriteria: The response completes every named part of the asking and receiving permission task using the supplied fictional or public case.
The response uses at least two accurate details from the lesson instruction and distinguishes evidence from assumption.
The response gives a safe, feasible next step or support route and does not depend on private disclosure, body comparison, or recorded media proof.
adaptationChoices: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required. Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
